title: OpenIddict
description: OpenIddict is a simple OpenID Connect server for ASP.NET Core. It is easier to set up than IdentityServer and is a good choice for lightweight authentication scenarios.

data.text: OpenIddict is an open-source OpenID Connect server for ASP.NET Core. It abstracts away the complexity of token validation and issuance while remaining fully compliant with OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0 standards.

data.title: Installation
data.content: Install OpenIddict and its ASP.NET Core integration.

data.title: Basic OpenIddict Setup

terms.definition: An identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0 for authenticating users.
The endpoint where clients exchange credentials for tokens.
An OAuth 2.0 grant type where the client sends a username and password directly to the token endpoint.

data.title: Use Authorization Code Flow
data.text: Password flow is shown for simplicity but is not recommended for public clients. Use Authorization Code flow with PKCE for browser and mobile apps.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: OpenIddict simplifies OpenID Connect server setup
It stores tokens using Entity Framework Core by default
data.takeaway: OpenIddict is a pragmatic choice for small to medium apps needing standards-based auth.

data.title: Exercise: Issue a Token
data.description: Configure OpenIddict and request a token using Postman.
steps: Create a new ASP.NET Core project and add OpenIddict
Configure the token endpoint and password flow
Use Postman to POST to /connect/token with grant_type=password
Decode the returned access token and verify the claims
data.expectedOutcome: OpenIddict issues a signed access token for valid credentials.
